title: When the Oath Falls
premise: Lena Dravenmoor was born in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, and bound by her mother's debt to the temple that keeps its records. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive seeking anyone touched by the gift, Lena discovers she carries a fragment of the old covenant between realms—a covenant her ancestors broke to make the Hollow safe. Hunted through a kingdom where memory itself is weaponized, she must gather the scattered oath-keepers and reforge the broken pact before the realms collapse into each other at the turning of the year. In the end, Lena pays the debt with her own remembered name, sealing the new covenant and winning belonging for both realms—at the cost of being forgotten by everyone she saved.
about_author: Rosalind Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval land charters before turning to fantasy. She writes about debts, documents, and the quiet violence of inherited obligations.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Establishes daily life in the Hollow: copying temple ledgers to work off her mother's debt, the strange stillness where magic cannot follow, and her habit of writing down things the valley forgets. Emotional beat: quiet longing beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ink and Interest
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The temple's High Registrar reveals her debt has tripled through 'administrative fees,' and offers an out: inform on any gifted person who seeks refuge in the Hollow. Emotional beat: the trap of institutional kindness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A wounded traveler named Corvin collapses at the valley's edge, muttering in a language of light; when Lena touches his blood-stained map, it glows—and so does her hand. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. He recognizes the glow as covenant-script and realizes Lena is an unwitting heir to the Oathkeepers. He begs her to hide him from the hunters already crossing the pass. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Crown's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Hunter-Captain Vess's POV. Introduces the crown's hunt and Vess's method: reading memories extracted from captured gifted folk. She learns a 'null-born' scribe in the Hollow may hold the covenant's keystone. Emotional beat: cold certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The High Registrar sells Lena out to Vess in exchange for the temple's tax exemption. Lena flees with Corvin through the orchards as hunters burn the archive—her life's work. Emotional beat: grief for a home that never truly held her.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Leaving the Hollow for the first time, magic floods back into the world around her—and into her. Overwhelming sensory awakening; Corvin teaches her to anchor herself with written words. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Journey toward the first Oathkeeper shrine; flashbacks reveal how Corvin's order broke the covenant generations ago to save themselves, dooming both realms to slow decay. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Memories for Sale
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the market city of Dunharrow, memory-brokers trade recollections like coin. Lena buys a stranger's memory of her mother and learns her mother once served the covenant too. Emotional beat: the ache of secondhand love.

chapters.title: Vess Closes In
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Using an extracted memory, Vess tracks them to Dunharrow. But interrogating a child witness, she glimpses what the covenant's breaking actually cost the smallfolk. Emotional beat: doubt planted in duty.

chapters.title: The Shrine Beneath the Mill
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They find the first shrine defiled, its keeper dead, but Lena's blood awakens a residual echo showing how the covenant was forged: three names, freely given, binding two realms. Emotional beat: awe at scale of what's been lost.

chapters.title: Company of the Marked
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. They gather surviving Oathkeepers: Sefa, a hedge-witch hiding as a cook; Old Bram, whose gift is remembering everything he'd rather forget; and Iyo, a boy who dreams the other realm. Emotional beat: found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. Frightened and manipulated by a hunter informant, Iyo reveals their route. Hunters ambush the waystation; Bram dies holding the door, his final gift flooding Lena with centuries of covenant-memory. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Weight of Remembering
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Carrying Bram's memories, Lena experiences the covenant's forging firsthand—and learns the third name required is always forgotten by all who love its bearer. Emotional beat: dawning horror at the price ahead.

chapters.title: Vess's Choice
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to burn Dunharrow's gifted quarter as an example, Vess refuses and is branded a traitor herself. She defects, bringing intelligence on the crown's true plan: not hunting magic, but harvesting it to break the veil entirely. Emotional beat: redemption sought, not granted.

chapters.title: The Turning Year
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. With winter solstice days away—the moment the realms will tear open—the company races to the First Altar in the mountains. Corvin confesses his order's full betrayal and asks Lena to decide his punishment. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: Storm on the Stair
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The crown's remaining hunters corner them on the mountain stair. Sefa falls buying time; Iyo's dream-gift holds a bridge of light just long enough. Emotional beat: courage measured in seconds.

chapters.title: The First Altar
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the altar, the ritual demands three freely given names—but only two remain willing. The veil begins to split; the other realm bleeds through, beautiful and starving. Emotional beat: the cliff-edge of choice.

chapters.title: When the Oath Falls
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax. Lena gives her name willingly, understanding the cost: to be forgotten by every soul she saves. The covenant reforges through her; the realms knit together; Vess and Corvin hold the circle as she dissolves from memory. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. The world is saved but no one remembers Lena—except Corvin, whose order's old gift lets him keep one forbidden memory. He finds her ledger pages, still bearing her handwriting no one can attribute. Emotional beat: grief as guardianship.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Scribe
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Rebuilding the valley, Vess establishes a free archive in the ruined temple. A quiet woman works there whom no one can quite place, content among records. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, belonging found sideways.

chapters.title: What Remains Written
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Epilogue. Nameless but whole, Lena reads the covenant's new lines and finds someone added hers in the margin: 'the scribe who paid.' Memory can be stolen, but ink endures. Emotional beat: hard-won hope—belonging beyond remembrance.
